ptarmigan: Any of three species of small grouse in the genus Lagopus found in subarctic tundra areas of North America and Eurasia.
pteranodon: A member of Pteranodon, a genus of large pterosaurs, the males of which had a bony crest on the back of the head.
pteridine: A bicyclic aromatic heterocycle consisting of fused pyrimidine and pyrazine rings.
pteridologist: A person who studies ferns and other pteridophytes.
pteridology: The scientific study of ferns and other pteridophytes.
pteridophyte: Any plant of the division Pteridophyta, of simple vascular plants that reproduce via spores rather than seeds and that alternate generations of diploid (sporophyte) and haploid…
pteridosperm: Any of various extinct gymnosperms, of the division Pteridospermatophyta, resembling ferns, but producing seeds instead of spores
pterin: A ketonic amide derivative of pteridine responsible for some of the colouring in nature.
pterodactyl: A pterosaur of the genus Pterodactylus.
pteropod: Any of free-swimming pelagic sea snails and sea slugs, of the suborder Thecosomata, that have winglike lobes on the feet; a sea butterfly.
pterosaur: Any flying reptile, of the extinct order †Pterosauria, including the pterodactyls.
pterygium: An abnormal mass of tissue in the corner of the eye that obstructs vision.
pterygoid: Of, pertaining to or lying in the region of the inferior part of the sphenoid bone of the vertebrate skull.
pteryla: One of the areas of a bird's skin on which feathers grow.
ptomaine: Any of various amines formed by putrefactive bacteria.
ptosis: The prolapse of a bodily organ, especially drooping of the eyelid or the breasts.
ptyalin: A form of amylase found in saliva that breaks down starch into maltose and dextrin.
